INCIDENT MARTCO #004 / After Hours

RECORD STATUS Incomplete — communications lost
INCIDENT SUMMARY

The records recovered from MARTCO Super Store #004 describe an ordinary night shift that stopped being ordinary somewhere between the closing announcement and the first scream.

In the days around the incident, the Malevorn area filled with reports nobody could explain: sudden violence, missing persons, animals that attacked without fear, and neighbors who stopped being themselves. Emergency services were overwhelmed within hours. Then the lines went quiet.

A few fragmented communications use one word for the affected: SCOURGEN.

The Scourgen are not the dead. They are living people and living animals, and every one of them is still alive. Each has been possessed by LEGION, which takes over a living mind and body and bends it to a single will. The possessed hunt together, flank together, and retreat together, because they are not many minds. They are one mind in many bodies: a hive, coordinated by Legion.

That is the part the people inside MARTCO never had the chance to piece together. All they could see was that the things in the aisles had once been customers, coworkers, and stray animals, that they were stronger, faster and more twisted than anything alive should be, and that they moved like they were listening to the same voice.

The employees had no explanation. They had a building to get out of, and something inside it was hunting them.

THE WIDER EVENT

The MARTCO incident happened during the same regional catastrophe tied to the impact near Malevorn. Later accounts would place Legion at the center of it.

What Legion is, no one has established. The records do not describe a ghost, a demon, or a spirit, and they do not describe a machine, an engineered organism, or a visitor from another world. Every attempt to name it falls short. It hijacks consciousness and living bodies to run its hive, and beyond that it is simply incomprehensible: not a thing that can be explained with the categories we have.

The people inside the store knew none of this. No surviving MARTCO record shows that anyone there understood Legion, or had any contact with the people at the center of the event.

MARTCO #004 was not the center of the catastrophe. It was one lit window in a very large dark.

LOCATION: MARTCO SUPER STORE #004

A big-box, twenty-four-hour supermarket. The sales floor runs eight departments deep: Snacks and Bakery, Wine & Spirits, Soda, Canned Goods, Breakfast, Home Goods and Electronics, with Fresh Produce and Floral & Garden down the west wall and Frozen Foods and Dairy & Eggs down the east. Six checkout lanes face the entrance. Customer Service sits in one front corner and the Pharmacy in the other.

Behind the sales floor is the part customers never see: the Stockroom, two receiving docks, the employee restrooms, the Manager’s Office, and the Security Office with its wall of camera feeds.

By the time the playable shift begins, the building is wrecked. Some lights hold. Others flicker or die. Carts, pallets and spilled stock choke the aisles. The back rooms are hard to see in and harder to leave.

The shutter over the front entrance is down. It is unclear whether that was a deliberate lockdown, a mechanical failure, or the wider emergency reaching into the building.

The public-address system still works. Its recordings keep cycling through ordinary announcements: closing reminders, department calls, cleanup requests, safety notices. They were written for a normal business day. They were not written for this.

SURVIVOR 001 — THE CLOSING MANAGER
NAME COLT
AGE 26
HEIGHT 5′11″
ROLE Closing manager, MARTCO #004
BUILD Average. Nothing special.
WEAPON Remington 700 chambered in .308 Winchester, his father's hunting rifle

Colt was the closing manager, the one who walks the floor at night, counts the drawers, kills the lights, and is the last name on the lock-up sheet. He is an all-around average man: no military past, no police training, no hidden talent. What he has is the building. He knows the sales floor, the employee corridors, the stockroom, and where the staff keep the things customers aren’t supposed to touch.

Colt kept his father’s old Remington 700 hunting rifle in his truck. It was never meant for a night like this. When the doors locked and the dead began moving, the familiar rifle was the one thing he could reach without having to search the store.

His priorities were simple. Stay alive. Find supplies. Keep moving. Make it to morning.

LAST KNOWN STATUS: Inside MARTCO #004 during the active incident. No verified extraction record has been recovered.

SURVIVOR 002 — THE CUSTOMER
NAME JUSTINE
AGE 22
HEIGHT 5′2″
ROLE Customer. College student.
BUILD Light, quick, hard to pin down
WEAPON M44 carbine, an old surplus rifle from World War II, recovered from a dead survivor

Justine was a college student who ran into MARTCO for a few groceries on her way home. She had no connection to the store and no reason to be there past closing. When the attack started she did what most people do: she hid. The surviving accounts place her in the rear corridors and employee-only areas at different points in the night, going quiet whenever something passed.

She is not the strongest person in the building. She is, by every account, one of the quickest. She slips between shelving and around corners that heavier people can’t. The M44’s bayonet gives her a last-resort answer when something gets too close, but she is less durable and less precise at distance.

She found the old M44 carbine on a dead survivor. Its folding bayonet turned out to suit her. There is no reliable evidence she had any combat training before that night.

LAST KNOWN STATUS: Inside MARTCO #004 during the active incident. No verified extraction record has been recovered.

BONUS FILE — THE MASCOT
NAME MARTY
AGE Unlisted. Mascots don’t age.
HEIGHT 6′2″ (cap included)
ROLE Official mascot, MARTCO Super Store
BUILD Round, fluffy, remarkably well-balanced
WEAPON Uzi. Fully automatic, 32 rounds per magazine. Source: unknown

A familiar face at MARTCO, Marty is the store's cheerful orange mascot. Recognizable by his oversized smile, red baseball cap, and white gloves, he's become something of a local institution. He has been greeting customers for as long as anyone can remember, and he has never once been caught without a smile.

Marty represents everything MARTCO stands for: friendly service, everyday savings, and making every shopping trip a pleasant experience. The brand guidelines describe him as “friendly, helpful, and always ready to lend a hand.” They do not mention a firearm. Staff are also reminded, in writing, that Marty is not a potato, a nugget, or a peach.

His exact responsibilities have never been particularly well documented, although he appears to take his position very seriously. His listed hobbies are waving, high-fives, and “aggressive customer service.” His shift history, badge number, and current whereabouts are all marked N/A.

LAST KNOWN STATUS: Approachable, dependable, and surprisingly well equipped.

MARTY'S MOTTO: Shop happy. Shop MARTCO. With Marty around, you're always getting a bang for your buck.

MARTCO — YOUR STORE. YOUR SAVINGS. YOUR MARTY.

THE NIGHT SHIFT

The playable record begins at about 10:00 PM. The objective is to stay alive until 6:00 AM.

The shift is a survival reconstruction assembled from incomplete accounts. Its waves and escalating encounters represent the pressure of the incident, not a minute-by-minute transcript.

Around 3:00 AM the records describe the arrival of a much larger organism that survivors called THE DRAGONAUT. It is far more dangerous than anything else in the building, and the records suggest Legion pushed it through the hive to hunt them directly. Later sightings were reported, and whether they were the same host, additional hosts, or panicked observations cannot be determined.

SURVIVE UNTIL 6:00 AM.

Morning is the objective. It is not a guarantee of rescue.

FIELD NOTES — SURVIVAL
  • CONSERVE AMMUNITION. Colt’s and Justine’s rifles hold five rounds each. Reloading takes time and attention.
  • KNOW THE BUILDING. Shelving, checkout lanes, stockroom racking and narrow corridors can help you or trap you.
  • REMEMBER THEY ARE ALIVE. The Scourgen are living hosts. Legion drives them as one, so expect them to come at you together.
  • PRESERVE YOUR LIGHT. The flashlight battery is limited. Use it when you can’t afford not to see.
  • SEARCH CAREFULLY. Supplies are scattered across the sales floor and back-of-house.
  • LISTEN TO THE PA. Most announcements are routine recordings. That they keep playing does not mean the store is safe.
  • KEEP YOUR DISTANCE FROM LARGE HOSTS. The Dragonaut is not an ordinary possessed.
  • COLT: tougher and more precise. His steadier aim rewards deliberate shots, but he cannot move as quickly and has no bayonet.
  • MARTY: the best at everything, with the only fully automatic weapon in the building: hold fire to spray. His Uzi holds 32 rounds, so mind the magazine.
  • JUSTINE: faster and equipped with a bayonet. She can reposition and defend herself up close, but has less health and a harder time landing shots at long range.
OUTCOME — UNRESOLVED

Colt and Justine are both documented inside MARTCO during the incident. The surviving material does not establish whether they escaped together, separated before the final loss of contact, or stayed inside after the record ends.

No authenticated rescue manifest has been found. No remains have been conclusively identified as either survivor.

Their ultimate fate remains UNKNOWN.

The store was one incident among many. The people inside it were never in a position to understand the whole disaster.
